claims.claim: A Western free reed is not simply 'blown closed'. Fletcher's 1979 inward/outward classification does not fit free reeds neatly; a free reed can show either closing or opening behaviour depending on conditions. A normal Western reed sounds only for p1 > p2 (one flow direction), and is usually described as blown-closed, but the companion reed on the other side of the plate in a harmonica channel is blown-open.

summary: Web fetch and curl were blocked by the sandbox allowlist, and the search tool hit a usage limit partway, so every source was read at snippet or abstract level only. Confirmed to exist: Millot-Baumann 2007, Ricot et al. 2005, St. Hilaire et al. 1971, Fletcher 1993, Tarnopolsky et al. 2000. Cantilever formula (coefficient 0.16154) and the input's 27-value length table verified by computation. The input's 'blown-closed (-,+), inward-striking' is only partly right: Western reeds are usually blown-closed but the companion reed is blown-open, and 'inward-striking' is a misnomer. Q values, 2 kPa threshold, 0.2/1.4-1.6 kPa LDV pressures, the S_u equation, materials, and synthesis models remain unverified. A follow-up pass with arxiv.org, hal.science, unsw.edu.au allowed is needed.
